title: After Bills win OT thriller, how concerning is Rams’ 2-3 start?
author: Nate Atkins
content:
The Athletic has live coverage of Bills vs. Rams in NFL ‘Monday Night Football.’

INGLEWOOD, Calif. — Tyler Bass drilled a 45-yard game-winning field goal in a wild, back-and-forth affair that saw the lead change eight times as the Buffalo Bills pulled off a 37-34 overtime victory over the Los Angeles Rams at SoFi Stadium on Monday night.

With the win, the Bills improve to 4-1, while the Rams fall to 2-3.

The Bills got the first crack in overtime and looked poised to score after driving downfield deep in Rams territory. But James Cook, who was having a monster game, fumbled the ball at the Rams’ 22-yard line after a vintage Nate Landman punchout.

Matthew Stafford and the Rams then drove 50 yards in eight plays and could have sealed the win with a 48-yard field goal by kicker Harrison Mevis. However, the Bills’ Gregory Rousseau blocked the kick, giving Buffalo new life.

Josh Allen immediately took advantage. His back-to-back 19- and 13-yard runs put the Bills in field goal range. Bass made the kick, and his teammates lifted him into the air to celebrate.

Both defenses played well early, but the teams began trading touchdowns in the second half. Allen, who completed just 12 passes, led three straight touchdown drives when his team needed it most.

With the game tied 27-27 and just over seven minutes remaining in the fourth quarter, the Bills went on an 11-play, 71-yard drive and capped it with a 5-yard touchdown by Cook with 1:39 to go, giving Buffalo a 34-27 lead. But the Rams weren’t done.

Stafford stormed downfield on an eight-play, 63-yard drive. Kyren Williams made an incredible one-handed third-down catch to get the ball down to the 1 and finished the possession with a 1-yard touchdown run to tie the game at 34-34 and ultimately force overtime.

Stafford threw three touchdown passes in the win, including two to wide receiver Davante Adams. Puka Nacua caught 17 passes on 24 targets for 138 yards and a touchdown.

Allen leaned on his legs, finishing with 121 rushing yards, while running back James Cook had 111 rushing yards and two touchdowns.

The Bills will next travel to Las Vegas to face the Raiders in Week 6. The Rams will look to get back on track with a home game against the Arizona Cardinals.
